We added a CDN and Tokyo users still waited on our Virginia origin.

Then we cached the wrong API response — and a user in Berlin briefly saw someone else's dashboard header.

CDN isn't a toggle. Here's what edge caching actually controls. 🧵

A CDN puts PoPs (edge servers) near users.

Cache HIT → edge returns stored bytes. Origin never touched.

Cache MISS → edge fetches origin, stores if cacheable, returns.

First request to each PoP can feel slower. Warm-up + TTL strategy matter.

Static vs dynamic — the first decision:

✅ Cache at edge: hashed JS/CSS, public images, anonymous HTML

❌ Don't: /api/me, session cookies, user-specific SSR

Rule: if two users must never share bytes, default to private, no-store at the shared edge.

HTTP headers drive CDN behavior — not the vendor logo.

Good static asset:
Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable

Authenticated API:
Cache-Control: private, no-store

Cookies in the response do NOT auto-prevent CDN caching.

Invalidation hierarchy:

1. Version URLs (app.[hash].js) → long TTL, no purge
2. Purge specific paths on deploy → automate in CI
3. Revalidate (304) → origin round trip, cheaper than full miss

Purge /* on every deploy = origin thundering herd.

Origin shield: regional edges miss → fetch shield PoP → shield misses once → origin.

One origin fill serves many edges. Worth it when origin is fragile or you purge often.
